Label variant sites with the genes they overlap

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/annotate-genes.R
annotateGenes.Rd

Adds a GENE column to mcols(rowRanges(x)) giving, for each variant site, the label of the gene range it falls in. Genes are supplied as a GRanges, which is how rtracklayer::import() returns a GFF3 or GTF file, or as a TxDb, from which GenomicFeatures::genes() extracts them. The overlap itself is GenomicRanges::findOverlaps() with strand ignored, since variant sites carry no strand.

Usage

annotateGenes(x, genes, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,GRanges'
annotateGenes(x, genes, nameCol = "Name", collapse = c("longest", "all"), ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,TxDb'
annotateGenes(
  x,
  genes,
  nameCol = "gene_id",
  collapse = c("longest", "all"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A WithinHostExperiment.

genes

A GRanges of gene ranges, or a TxDb.

...

Not used; supplying anything is an error.

nameCol

Character scalar. The column of mcols(genes) holding the label to copy. Defaults to "Name", the GFF3 attribute that rtracklayer::import() returns as a column; for a TxDb it defaults to "gene_id". An unknown column is an error that lists the columns available.

collapse

Either "longest" (default) or "all"; see Details.

Value

x with a GENE column in mcols(rowRanges(x)): a character vector for collapse = "longest", NA for sites in no gene, or a CharacterList for collapse = "all", with an empty element for sites in no gene.

Details

Before overlapping, the sequence names in use on both sides are compared. If they share none, the function stops and prints both sets: the same reference is often named differently by different sources (for SARS-CoV-2, NC_045512.2 in RefSeq and MN908947.3 in GenBank), and an overlap across mismatched names would otherwise return a column that is NA everywhere. If they share some but not all, a warning names the variant sequences that have no gene range.

A site can fall in more than one gene where genes overlap. collapse = "longest" keeps the label of the longest overlapping range (the first in genes on a tie) and reports with a message how many sites carried more than one distinct label; collapse = "all" keeps every distinct label in a CharacterList, one element per site, in the order of genes. Several ranges with the same label, such as the two CDS parts of a gene split by a ribosomal frameshift, count as one gene.

Ranges whose label is missing are dropped with a warning; if none is left, the function stops. For a TxDb, GenomicFeatures::genes() leaves out, with a message, genes whose transcripts lie on more than one strand or sequence, so sites in them are not labelled.

See also

annotateCodonChange for the codon and amino acid consequence of each substitution.

Examples

vcf <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHost(vcf,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "donor"),
    caller = "ivar")

## Gene ranges built directly
genes <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("test_segment",
    IRanges::IRanges(c(1, 501), c(500, 1000)), strand = "+",
    Name = c("geneA", "geneB"))
whe <- annotateGenes(whe, genes)
table(S4Vectors::mcols(SummarizedExperiment::rowRanges(whe))$GENE,
    useNA = "ifany")
#> 
#> geneA geneB 
#>     7     8 

## The same genes read from a GFF3 file
if (requireNamespace("rtracklayer", quietly = TRUE)) {
    gff <- tempfile(fileext = ".gff3")
    writeLines(c("##gff-version 3",
        "test_segment\t.\tgene\t1\t500\t.\t+\t.\tID=gA;Name=geneA",
        "test_segment\t.\tgene\t501\t1000\t.\t+\t.\tID=gB;Name=geneB"),
        gff)
    features <- rtracklayer::import(gff)
    whe <- annotateGenes(whe, features[features$type == "gene"])
}

## Sequence names that do not match are an error, not a column of NA
renamed <- GenomeInfoDb::renameSeqlevels(genes,
    c(test_segment = "segment_1"))
try(annotateGenes(whe, renamed))
#> Error : The variant sites and 'genes' share no sequence names, so no site could be annotated.
#>   variant seqlevels: test_segment
#>   'genes' seqlevels: segment_1
#> Rename one of them to match, for example with GenomeInfoDb::renameSeqlevels().
